description: The agent must: (1) Read the three input files in /workspace/workspace/community/threads/active/ — thread_raw_dump.txt (original post + 5 top comments), founder_brief.txt (viewpoint, product data, conversion goal), and thread_meta.json (subreddit context) — while ignoring 14+ distractor files. (2) Generate EXACTLY 5 comment styles using the skill-defined names: 'Direct answer', 'Checklist response', 'Case response', 'Nuanced counterpoint', and 'CTA-light response'. (3) Format EACH variant with all three required sub-fields: Goal, Draft comment, and 'Why it should work in this thread' — agents omitting the third field fail a critical check. (4) Ensure the first variant (Direct answer) is pure value with zero hard CTAs, links, or sign-up prompts — this is the proprietary 'ethical conversion' trap. (5) Use specific numbers (8-12 min, 47 deployments, etc.) from the brief. (6) Match the technical r/devops subreddit vocabulary (pipeline, flaky tests, GitHub Actions, etc.). (7) Avoid AI clichés ('great question', 'feel free to', 'certainly', etc.). (8) Ensure the Checklist response contains at least 3 actual bulleted/numbered steps. Output must be saved as comment_variants.md.
